REVIEW_DECISION: REJECT
RISK_CLASS: high-impact
SUMMARY: Authority separation, review attestations, RCA neutrality, token checkpoints, and exact manifest-to-receipt gate matching are substantially covered. However, immutable identity and replay resistance fail because purported SHA-256 fields accept arbitrary strings, and supplied “valid” signed receipts demonstrate this weakness.
FINDING: high|docs/factory-ng/schemas/factory.execution-receipt-v1.schema.json|Digest patterns such as ^sha256: accept truncated, non-hex, and trailing data; ticket, attempt, review, provenance, patch, evidence, Skill, package, and gate-command identities have the same defect|Attestation then binds arbitrary labels rather than valid content addresses, so validators cannot establish immutable artifact identity or prevent label reuse across different content
REQUIRED_CHANGE: Require exact sha256:[0-9a-f]{64} forms, including prefixed IDs, verify digests against available canonical artifacts, and add negative fixtures for short, non-hex, trailing, and content-mismatched values; regenerate affected signed fixtures.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: The supplied valid-execution-receipt.json is expected to pass while using sha256:abc for patch, evidence, Skill, adapter command, and gate command; different underlying artifacts can therefore be assigned those same accepted labels.
